items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: And this lady, Anna Kisselegoff -- I should bring you the copy of the writeup.

ctx.x: And one of our dancers in this show -- he's a tap dancer known as Sad Man Sims, you see. And he had one of our partner's names which was Howards. So anyhow, he did an on the town dance, Raymond Kaleland. Now the next one comes out, you see (unintelligible) see, and he does an on the town dance, you see. And that's what it was reminiscing with Chuck Green was all about on the town, you see. And that's the only kind of out of town trade and so forth and so on, see, and they was trying to keep public relations on…

And it become what they called -- the critics finally wrote about it. They said it was a sleeper hit, you know. And this lady, Anna Kisselegoff -- I should bring you the copy of the writeup. I should have had it to you before, you know. But that's what it all consisted of, you know. And some film company was -- had some kind of apprentice, you know, a fellow named Russell Schwartz. And his staff. And they was -- had been

up to Hunter's College, you know, to show you how the spirit can move, you see. And at that time he was alive -- Professor Marshall Sterns, you see. But he was compiling. He had to be off and away, you know, him and Jean.
